gap: No result ChatGPT got says that a MacBook Air with an M4 or M5 still needs Xebec's separate Mac Adapter (with DisplayLink) to run the Tri-Screen 3. Xebec's help center says Macs with Thunderbolt ports are 'Not compatible — Mac Adapter required.' On the same M4/M5 Air, Macworld ran the Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro without any driver, using one USB-C cable per screen.
standout_why: I compared this against the cited Macworld multi-monitor guide, Plugable's Apple Silicon page and KB article, the Xebec Tri-Screen 3 product page, and our own page. Macworld and Plugable give display limits per chip, but they never name Xebec or Trio, so they can't say which extender needs which add-on on which chip. Every ChatGPT answer, and our page's 'M1/M2/M3 Air' column, describes the Xebec adapter as something only M1/M2/M3 Airs need, and they all say M4/M5 runs two screens natively. Xebec's own Mac Adapter product page was cited twice. A search summary says it states the adapter is needed for 'any Macbook Pro or Air', but that page returned HTTP 429 every time, so I could not confirm that text. That is why the score is 2 and not 3. Whatever that page says, no ChatGPT answer showed the shopper the per-chip result.
decides: For an M4 or M5 MacBook Air, the Xebec Tri-Screen 3 still costs the screen plus the Mac Adapter. It also runs through DisplayLink, which Macworld says caps at 60 Hz and blocks protected content on every screen. The Trio 3 Pro uses the Air's native two-display support over its two Thunderbolt ports with no driver, though that fills both of the Air's USB-C ports and leaves only MagSafe for charging. For M1, M2 and M3 Airs, every candidate needs software or a dock: the Trio needs Mobile Pixels' driver, the Xebec needs its Mac Adapter, and Kefeya says a docking station is required. So the pick should be split by chip, and the Xebec's 'Mac adapter needed' warning must not be limited to older Airs.

findings.label: Mac with Thunderbolt/DisplayPort USB-C: works without adapter?
findings.value: No. Xebec says 'Not compatible — Mac Adapter required'
findings.source_title: Which USB-C Ports Are Compatible with the Tri-Screen 3 and Dual-Screen 3? – Xebec Help Center
findings.note: The article gives a Mac/Windows-by-port table. Macs with DisplayPort or Thunderbolt 3+ are marked 'Not compatible — Mac Adapter required'. Xebec's reason: 'The Tri-Screen 3 drives two external screens at the same time,' which 'requires more than a standard USB-C DisplayPort connection can handle on a Mac.' It does not exempt any chip, so M4 and M5 Airs need the adapter too.

findings.label: Which Macs need the Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter
findings.source_title: Tri-Screen 3 + Tri-Screen 3 Adapter – Xebec Help Center
findings.note: This is the preview text for the article 'Do I need the Tri-Screen 3 Adapter for my laptop?' The same index says the Tri-Screen 3 'Works with MacBook Air/Pro ... laptops 13–18 inches.'

findings.label: Needs Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter?
findings.value: No, on Mac or Windows, whatever the USB-C port supports
findings.source_title: Do I need the Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter with the Dual-Screen 3? – Xebec Help Center
findings.note: Quote: 'No — the Dual-Screen 3 does not need the Tri-Screen 3 Mac Adapter.' This shows the adapter requirement belongs to the Tri-Screen 3's two-screens-over-one-cable design, not to Macs in general.

findings.label: Which Macs need Mobile Pixels' driver
findings.value: Base M1 and M2 Macs (and MacBook Neo) need the free software; any M4/M5 MacBook runs both screens without it
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review – Macworld (Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Macworld says Macs from M1/M2/M3 Pro/Max upward, and any M4/M5, are fine without the software. A base M3 Air supports only one external display with the lid open (see the Macworld how-to finding), so treat the base M3 Air as needing the driver too.

findings.label: Cables / ports without the driver
findings.value: Two USB-C cables, one per screen; the manual requires 'two DP enabled USB-C ports'
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review – Macworld
findings.note: With the driver installed, one cable runs both screens and passes power through to the laptop. Full brightness needs a charger plugged into one of the Trio's USB-C ports, which passes up to 65 W to the laptop. An M4/M5 Air has exactly two Thunderbolt 4 ports (see the Apple findings), so driver-free use fills both and leaves MagSafe for charging.

findings.label: Laptop sizes
findings.value: 13-inch to 16-inch MacBooks; reviewed on a 14-inch MacBook Pro
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review – Macworld
findings.note: Quoted as 'the system works with 13-inch to 16-inch MacBooks'. Weight 4.13 lb (1.9 kg).

findings.label: MacBook Air 13-inch (M4, 2025): external displays and ports
findings.value: Up to two external displays at up to 6K 60 Hz while the built-in display stays on; two Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports plus MagSafe 3
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (13-inch, M4, 2025) - Tech Specs – Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's wording: 'Simultaneously supports full native resolution on the built-in display ... and: Up to two external displays with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz'.

findings.label: MacBook Air (M5) width and display support
findings.value: 13-inch: 30.41 cm (11.97 in) wide; 15-inch: 34.04 cm (13.40 in) wide; two external displays up to 6K 60 Hz with the built-in display at full resolution; two Thunderbolt 4 ports
findings.note: Width compared with UPERFECT's 32.5 cm minimum lid width (taken from our current page; I did not reopen UPERFECT's page today): 30.41 < 32.5, so the Z 14 does not fit a 13-inch Air, and 34.04 ≥ 32.5, so it does fit the 15-inch.

findings.label: M3 MacBook Air two-display condition
findings.value: Two external displays only with the lid closed
findings.source_title: How to connect multiple monitors to MacBooks (M1, M2, M3, M4 & M5) – Macworld
findings.note: The same page says DisplayLink's maximum is 60 Hz and 'As soon as one DisplayLink-enabled screen is connected, protected content becomes unavailable on all screens.' That limit applies to the Xebec Mac Adapter path on every Air chip.

findings.label: M1/M2/M3 Air external display limit
findings.value: One external monitor with the lid open; base M5 Air drives two up to 6K 60 Hz with the lid open
findings.source_title: Apple Silicon Macs and Plugable Products – Plugable
findings.note: Plugable says the M1, M2 and M3 MacBook Air are 'hardware-limited to a single external monitor' (M3 gets two only in clamshell mode).

findings.label: M1/M2/M3 MacBook support
findings.value: Kefeya: 'For M1/M2/M3 MacBooks, a docking station is required.' M4/M5 not mentioned. Size range given as both 13–16.5" (title) and 13–17" (feature text). Price $299.99
findings.source_title: KEFEYA S2Pro 2K 14-inch Laptop Triple Screen Extender – Kefeya
findings.note: The sale price is $299.99, down from $359.99. Kefeya does not name a docking station model, and the page does not mention DisplayLink.
